Ellen (AM): Heads-up: BrightArc wants to move POC to a 12mo commit. They need reserved GPUs for predictable latency, autoscale runway for product launches, and an enforceable monthly burst spend cap. Procurement also asked for KMS + 1y audit retention answers.

Marcus (SE): Do we have their traffic profile? qps, burst length, token sizes?

Ellen (AM): Short summary from the customer: steady 110 qps, two scheduled marketing blasts/week up to ~1.8k qps for 90-180s, nightly embedding batch of ~150 jobs. Typical chat: 130 input tokens / 100 output tokens. Targets: p95 < 200ms, p99 < 420ms.

Dev (SRE): Ops suggestion: reserve baseline GPUs to cover the 110 qps at p95, plus a burst runway that uses autoscale, quantized burst replicas, and cross-AZ spread. Preheat KV cache 10-15min ahead of expected blasts. We'll also implement a tenant-level hard cap and automated fallback chain.

Tori (Sales Eng): Need a simple committed vs burst pricing slide: (A) committed reserved GPUs + platform fee; (B) committed + pre-purchased burst credits with hard cap; (C) private deployment license. Also they want an example invoice and worst-case burst billing.

Marcus (SE): Quick sizing from bench (decoder int8): conservative steady throughput ~40 qps/GPU @ p95 for ~230 token seq without heavy batching. With KV caching and modest batching that moves toward ~70 qps/GPU, but commit math should be conservative. So 110 qps -> 3 reserved GPUs (110/40 = 2.75 -> 3).

Marcus (SE): Burst delta = 1800 - 110 = 1690 qps. If same model @40 qps/GPU -> ~43 GPUs. Practical plan: reserved 3 + burst runway using quantized burst replicas at ~100 qps/GPU and aggressive batching -> ~17 GPUs for peak. Recommend offering X GPU-minutes of burst credits per month and an optional hard cap.

Dev (SRE): Preheat playbook (short): T-15m run kv-warm to populate common prefixes; T-10m synthetic ramp to validate p95; T-2m enable aggressive batching window. Example warm command we use in staging: ./warm --target 1600 --concurrency 200 --seq 230 --duration 120

Dev (SRE): Degradation ladder when cap reached: full model -> quantized model -> shorten outputs -> deny non-critical embedding jobs. We'll document expected SLOs and tail impact per step. Also recommend cross-AZ placement and spot fallback for non-critical burst capacity.

Tori (Sales Eng): On burst-cap mechanics: propose two options to customer: (1) pre-purchased burst credits (cheaper per GPU-minute) with configurable tenant hard cap; (2) pay-as-you-go beyond credits at a premium. Include an alerting + hard stop option that triggers the fallback ladder.

Ellen (AM): Security Qs: customer needs CMK for at-rest encryption of inputs/outputs and 12 month audit retention with SIEM export. They asked whether Private VPC shortens procurement timeline for PHI.

Dev (SRE): We support customer-managed KMS keys and audit log export to SIEM. Private VPC + BAA reduces data surface for procurement; on-prem is possible but adds license and integration work. I'll attach the infra checklist in the runbook.

Marcus (SE): Action items: I'll produce a one-page capacity calc (assumptions + GPU counts) and a sample cost table (committed vs burst vs pay-as-you-go). Tori: please draft the pricing slide and contract snippet for burst credits and hard cap. Dev: add KV warm script and security checklist to the runbook. Ellen: collect procurement contacts and legal asks.

cap-bot: Created ticket POC-20456 "BrightArc commit: reserve 3 GPUs + burst runway + CMK & hard cap" assigned to @Marcus @Dev @Tori.

Ellen (AM): Let's sync in 45 to finalize before we send the procurement pack. :thumbsup:

Marcus (SE): Available.

Dev (SRE): On it.

Tori (Sales Eng): Will draft slides now.
